description: What a copy of a row says in its formulas. A fresh workbook: B1 =A1*2, C1 =$A$1+A$1+$A1, D1 =A2, then Rows("1:1").Copy(Rows("2:3")), once straight over rows 2 and 3 and once after Rows("2:3").Insert(); every formula read back through Range.Formula. Each copy is the source with its relative references moved down by its distance from the source, absolute ones kept; after an insert the copy is taken from the source as the insert left it (D1 is =A4 by then).
probe: a one-off COM script: Workbooks.Add, Range.Formula, Rows().Insert(), Rows().Copy(Destination), no clipboard
openClass: headless COM (DisplayAlerts off), a workbook created in the session, never saved
